findings.problem: The round-1 fix for the scientific-notation definition added a false condition. In school mathematics, whole numbers are $0, 1, 2, 3, \dots$, so negative values are excluded. Scientific notation needs $n$ to be an integer, which can be negative. The lesson's own next sentence gives $4.5 \times 10^{-6}$ as valid scientific notation, and the prefix list uses $10^{-2}$ to $10^{-9}$. A student who uses the stated definition would reject every value below $1$ written in scientific notation, such as $3.2 \times 10^{-4}$, which is a standard 'which is in scientific notation' item.
findings.source: OpenStax Elementary Algebra 2e, Section 6.7 (scientific notation: $a \times 10^n$ with $1 \le a < 10$ and $n$ an integer); OpenStax Prealgebra 2e, Section 1.1 (whole numbers are the counting numbers and zero)
